q:
It just hurts so much to hear the poor little guy cry himself to sleep.   
But I just need him to sleep so I can take a shower... 

Am I hurting him by doing this?
cx: Parent of a 10-month-old who falls asleep within five minutes when left in the cot for naps.

q: We got a sleep consultant and for a brief moment it felt like everything clicked – we had a few nights of 6–7 hour stretches with just one feed and it was honestly life changing.
cx: First-time mother of a 4-month-old in the UK.

q: Now it’s slipping again. We’re back to waking every 2-3 hours. Not the worst it’s ever been, but after seeing what he can do, it feels so discouraging.
cx: Same mother after the consultant's plan.

q: His crying is SO loud I can hear it from anywhere in the house (even with earplugs), so my husband taking shifts doesn’t really work and I feel awful about the neighbours too.
cx: Same mother.

q: I always imagined having more than one child but right now I’m honestly scared I couldn’t go through this again.
cx: Same mother.

q: Thanks we did lots of googling when the same thing happened at 3-3.5 months before we got the sleep consultant.
cx: Same mother replying to a commenter's regression explanation.

q: Unfortunately we don’t have a spare room and have slowly been wearing our sofa down when we were doing shifts and sleeping separately.
cx: Same mother.

q: We’ve have tried 5 - mam, tomee tippee, Philips avent, frigg and nuby, and he’s not liked any of them
cx: Same mother on dummy brands.

q: I had an overseas work call that lasted until almost midnight, and then she woke us up again at 4am on the dot. Tried Ferber again, and she just kept yelling. At some point I decided to just let her cry it out.
cx: Parent of a 2-year-old waking for the day at 3:30–4:30 for six weeks.

q: She cried for about 20min, which was hard, but she did fall asleep again. I felt bad the next day, but honestly I don’t know what to do anymore.
cx: Same parent.

q: daycare would tell me that she was so tired that she could barely stay up until nap time
cx: Same parent, on the days she got her up at 4am.

q: I’m also wondering if we’ve been ‘supporting’ her in this habit by running in right away and repeatedly.
cx: Same parent the morning after.

q: all the advice online is making my mind go all crazy I feel like I’m doing everything wrong and absolutely nothing right if I say my Bub slept badly people just keep providing advice which I understand is helpful and I’m all for advice but it’s like what do you take what do you leave.
cx: Solo parent of a 6-month-old in a sleep regression (also posted to r/beyondthebump).

q: I feel like half a person right now, it’s also just me and I feel so lonely and I just need space…I just need to be me but I’m not me anymore without my baby
cx: Same parent.

q: How can i push her morning wake later without her getting overtired at bedtime? My math is not mathing you guys!
cx: Parent of an almost-9-month-old waking at 5:40 sharp; uses Napper.

q: I know these early wakes and short naps usually  mean they need more awake time, but i keep wondering how much?
cx: Same parent.

q: So our 6 month old had been seeing pretty good progress with Ferber. Not always linear but by night 7 he was basically going through the night with maybe 1 or 2 quick protest cries.
cx: Father on night 8, when the baby woke with a cold.

q: I’m still scared to undo everything or that we undid everything. Sometimes it’s hard to know when to intervene or when not to and mess up the training.
cx: Same father after rocking the sick baby to sleep.

q: He also wants to be up for the day at 5am and refuses to nap, so it’s ALL day. I’ve tried everything to fix his sleep and nothing is working.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of a 7-month-old finishing a degree.

q: I have exams that are due Friday and the only option I have to do them is to stay up until midnight
cx: Same mother.

q: My husband is gone at work from 4am-6pm and he also cooks dinner and we share bedtime. I begged him to call in today because I just need a break but he wouldn’t.
cx: Same mother.

q: My mom got a PHD while working and raising four children, so why the fuck am I struggling this much being a SAHM while earning a bachelor’s degree?
cx: Same mother.

q: I have read precious little sleep and stupidly tried asking ChatGPT for help.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of 8-month-old twins nursed to sleep together.

q: I’m coming up to the end of my maternity leave and know that we need to kick this in the butt so they don’t have an awful time transitioning.
cx: Same mother.

q: With all the information at my disposal it feels overwhelming and I don’t know what the right method is.
cx: Same mother, weighing CIO or Ferber.

q: I’m just terrified of starting because during any of my attempts so far they do not slowly lessen their crying they escalate.
cx: Same mother.

q: He is currently in the chair method/pick up put down method. It’s been going great.
cx: Parent of an almost-9-month-old, day three, before a hard 4am waking.

q: I have posted in here about 5 times and nothing seems to work…
cx: Breastfeeding mother of an almost-7-month-old, training bedtime since 5.5 months.

q: Her naps are capped at 2 hours as suggested by this subreddit after looking for help.
cx: Same mother.

q: Then I had one week after she dropped to two naps where she didn’t cry before bed and only woke up twice. Then it just all randomly derailed.
cx: Same mother.

q: I feel like I’ve tried every trick in the book and she just cannot be sleep trained.
cx: Same mother.

q: I tracked sleep in the beginning of sleep training but I started going kind of crazy/obsessive from it so I stopped.
cx: Same mother when a commenter asks for her sleep log.

q: Yeah… the number just isn’t working 🥴 the last two days I’ve kept her up 11 hours (3/4/4) and its made relatively no difference.
cx: Same mother two days after following commenters' longer wake windows.

q: Oh and she is fussy all day long 🫠
cx: Same mother.

q: We also use huckleberry for wake windows and nap times.
cx: Parent of a 9-week-old awake for hours after an hour of night sleep (cross-posted).

q: Historically she was sleep trained (Ferber method) at 9 months old. At 18 months old we took her to Fiji (a huge time change for us) and when we returned the sleep training was ruined.
cx: Nursing mother of a just-turned-2-year-old (cross-posted to r/sleeptrain).

q: I tried for 2 weeks to get her back to sleeping independently and eventually gave up.
cx: Same mother.

q: About a 1.5 months ago she started sleeping through the night again. No change in routine she just started sleeping for 10-11 hrs in her crib all night. I thought wow we’re back baby!
cx: Same mother, before the night of the second birthday.

q: All of this to say: do I just give up on the crib entirely and move her into a big kid bed?
cx: Same mother.
